function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a set of “ready‑to‑paste” snippets you can drop into your repository.  
I’ve made a few reasonable assumptions about the project (see the notes at the end of each section).  

---

## 1️⃣ Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# File: Dockerfile
FROM node:18-alpine AS builder

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Install dependencies
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Build (if needed)
# RUN npm run build   # Uncomment if you have a build step

# Runtime stage
FROM node:18-alpine

# Create non‑root user
RUN addgroup -S app && adduser -S app -G app
USER app

# Set working directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy built artifacts from builder
COPY --from=builder /app .

# Expose port
EXPOSE 3000

# Start command
CMD ["node", "index.js"]
```

> **Assumptions**  
> * The entry point is `index.js` (adjust if it’s something else).  
> * The app listens on port **3000** – change the `EXPOSE` line if it differs.  
> * No build step is required; comment out the `npm run build` line if you do have one.  

---

## 2️⃣ Kubernetes YAML

### Deployment + Service

```yaml
# File: k8s/deployment.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: ghcr.io/your-org/nodejs-welcome:latest   # <-- replace with your registry & tag
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
        env:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80
    targetPort: 3000
```

> **Notes**  
> * Replace `ghcr.io/your-org/nodejs-welcome:latest` with the actual image name/tag you’ll push to.  
> * I chose `LoadBalancer` so the service is externally reachable; switch to `ClusterIP` or `NodePort` if you prefer.  
> * The service maps external port **80** to internal port **3000** (the port exposed by the Dockerfile).  

---

## 3️⃣ GitHub Actions Workflow

```yaml
# File: .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
name: Build & Push Docker Image

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  build-and-push:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write   # Needed for GHCR

    steps:
    - name: Checkout repository
      uses: actions/checkout@v4

    - name: Set up Docker Buildx
      uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v3

    - name: Log in to GitHub Container Registry
      uses: docker/login-action@v3
      with:
        registry: ghcr.io
        username: ${{ github.actor }}
        password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

    - name: Build and push Docker image
      uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
      with:
        context: .
        file: ./Dockerfile
        push: true
        tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/nodejs-welcome:latest
```

> **What this does**  
> * Triggers on pushes to `main`.  
> * Builds the image defined by the Dockerfile.  
> * Pushes it to GitHub Container Registry under the same name as the repo (`nodejs-welcome`).  
> * Uses the automatically supplied `GITHUB_TOKEN` for authentication.  

---

## 4️⃣ Adding & Pushing Changes

Because I don’t have direct access to your local environment, you’ll need to run the following commands yourself:

```bash
git add Dockerfile k8s/deployment.yaml .github/workflows/docker-build.yml
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, K8s manifests, and CI workflow"
git push origin main
```

If you’re using a different branch or want to tag the release, adjust the branch names or add a `--tags` flag accordingly.

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|---|------|
| ✅ | Dockerfile (in repo root) |
| ✅ | Kubernetes manifests (e.g., `k8s/deployment.yaml`) |
| ✅ | GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/docker-build.yml`) |
| ✅ | Commit & push to `main` |

Feel free to tweak the values (ports, image names, replica counts, etc.) to match your exact setup. Happy deploying!
